newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-U.S. rate worries dominate, Eurobourses down.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-U.S. rate worries dominate, Eurobourses down.

text.p: British, German and French stocks were all marked lower in early business on Monday amid cautious trade ahead of an important U.S. interest rate meeting on Tuesday.
On the currency markets, the dollar was steady, with trading volumes low in the absence of the Tokyo market, which was closed on Monday for a holiday.

However, the mark lost further ground against other European currencies, particularly the French franc, following the weekend European finance ministers' meeting in Dublin as the drive towards monetary union gathered pace.
On Friday the mark slipped to a two-month low against the French franc. It weakened further to a 3-1/2 month low early Monday at around 3.3810 francs.
But, as with the stock markets, the rate-setting meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Markets Committee was also overhanging the currency trading:

"Having ridden on the crest of a wave of optimism about EMU prospects, foreign exchange markets will shift their attention back to monetary policy this week, with the key event clearly being the FOMC meeting on Tuesday," said Klaus Baader, currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
A Reuter survey last week showed that 17 of 30 economists polled thought the FOMC meeting would raise rates but few in the market were talking about an increase bigger than one quarter percent.
Meanwhile, leading London stocks were down more than half a percent in value by 0900 gmt.
Traders said the market was unlikely to make any major move before a regular British rate-setting meeting on Monday and Tuesday's FOMC were out of the way.
"People will just be sitting tight desparately keen to keep out of trouble," said one trader.

Any pressure for a rate increase from Bank of England Governor Eddie George at the British policy discussion was likely to be rebuffed by Chancellor (finance minister) Kenneth Clarke, analysts said. A Reuters poll of 20 economists found a unanimous verdict of no change in rates.
On Friday, the blue chip FTSE 100 index closed down 10 points after hitting an intraday peak of 3,994.1 in early trade -- just short of the psychologically-important 4,000 level.
In Frankfurt, the DAX index opened trade lower and dealers said buying was on hold before ahead of a U.S. interest rates decision.
And on the Paris bourse shares started also lower on profit-taking with dealers cautious about U.S. rates and because of book squaring on the last day of the September accounting period.
Dealers said the firming of the French franc against the mark was not helping shares.
CURRENCIES AT 0900 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5165 marks and 109.80 yen compared with 1.5141 marks and 109.76 yen in Europe late on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 0900 GMT
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was down 27.3 points lower at 3,936.8.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 6.85 at 2,072.61.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was down 14.45 at 2,631.65 PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was slightly weaker in early Europe at $381.25 compared with a close at $381.75 on Friday.
